title: Image Captioning - Observability
description: DA3408 A4. Health, throughput/latency, client breakdown and system resources of the CPU image-captioning app.

panels.title: Captioning app
panels.description: Status: is Prometheus able to scrape the Streamlit app? Blue = UP, orange-red = DOWN (the word is shown as well, so it does not rely on colour).

panels.title: node_exporter
panels.description: Status: is the host metrics exporter reachable?

panels.title: Model loaded
panels.description: Status: 1 once the BLIP weights are in memory.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Number of alert rules currently firing (see Alertmanager at :9093).

panels.title: Active requests
panels.description: Requests being handled right now (single + bulk).

panels.title: Failed images (last 5 min)
panels.description: Share of images that errored over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Throughput (images per second, by mode)
panels.description: Subtitle: successful images per second, 1 min-ish rate. Story: bulk uploads show up as long plateaus, single uploads as short blips. Linear scale.

panels.title: Inference latency percentiles (seconds per image)
panels.description: Subtitle: p50 / p95 / p99 of model time per image. Story: the gap between p50 and p99 widens when the CPU is busy with a bulk job. Linear scale.

panels.title: Inference latency distribution (heatmap)
panels.description: Subtitle: how many images fell into each latency bucket over time. Story: a single bright band means steady latency; spreading upwards means slowdowns. Colour = images per interval (Cividis, colour-blind safe).

panels.title: Average time per request (log scale)
panels.description: Subtitle: mean end-to-end request time from the Summary (sum / count). Story: a bulk ZIP takes orders of magnitude longer than a single image, hence the log10 axis.

panels.title: Errors per minute (by type)
panels.description: Subtitle: failed images by exception type. Story: a corrupt upload or bad ZIP shows up here before users complain.

panels.title: Image size and caption length
panels.description: Subtitle: average input resolution (megapixels, right axis) and caption length (characters, left axis). Story: shows whether slow requests simply come from bigger images.

panels.title: Images processed per client IP (since app start)
panels.description: Subtitle: top 10 client IPs by images processed. Story: tells you who is generating the load. Bars are labelled with the value, not just colour.

panels.title: Requests per session (since app start)
panels.description: Subtitle: top 10 browser sessions by number of uploads.

panels.title: Images processed per browser (since app start)
panels.description: Subtitle: which browsers clients use (from the User-Agent).

panels.title: Host CPU usage (%)
panels.description: Subtitle: share of CPU time not idle, all cores averaged. Story: climbs during bulk uploads, because the model uses all cores. Linear, 0-100 %.

panels.title: Host memory used (%)
panels.description: Subtitle: memory in use (total minus available) and what the captioning process alone holds. Story: the app's footprint is mostly the model weights, so it barely moves with load.

panels.title: Disk space used on / (%)
panels.description: Subtitle: filesystem usage of the root mount. Linear, 0-100 %.

panels.title: Disk throughput (bytes per second)
panels.description: Subtitle: read and write traffic summed over all disks. Story: bulk ZIPs are read from memory, so this mostly shows model loading and logging.

panels.title: Network throughput (bytes per second)
panels.description: Subtitle: traffic on real interfaces (loopback and container bridges excluded).

panels.title: Throughput vs host CPU
panels.description: Subtitle: images/s (left axis) against CPU busy % (right axis). Story: CPU rises as soon as throughput starts and flat-lines near 100 % during bulk jobs: the app is CPU-bound.

panels.title: p95 latency vs host CPU
panels.description: Subtitle: p95 inference time (left axis) against CPU busy % (right axis). Story: when CPU saturates the tail latency grows - the user-visible cost of load.

panels.title: Concurrency vs host CPU
panels.description: Subtitle: requests in flight and images queued for the model (left axis) against CPU busy % (right axis). Story: a queue building up while CPU is pinned means the machine, not the code, is the bottleneck.

panels.title: App CPU share vs host CPU
panels.description: Subtitle: CPU used by the Streamlit process and total host CPU, both as % of the whole machine. Story: the gap between the lines is other work on the laptop.
